name: U-skate world
description: Gray-Scott at F = 0.062, k = 0.0609, Robert Munafo's 'U-skate world'. Here the excited uniform state (pale) is the stable background, and structures are holes in it: still negatons (dots), negative worms, and the U-skate — a U-shaped hole that glides closed end first at about 1.9 px per 1000 steps, in any direction (it isn't locked to the grid). The U-skate is a knife-edge object: at k ≈ 0.0610 it slowly stretches into a worm, at k ≈ 0.06085 it collapses into a single negaton. Here three skates meet and freeze into a still cluster of six negatons. Things to try: place the U-skate stamp (rotate it to aim); paint k a little higher to make a skate grow a tail, or lower to stop it dead; the erase brush punches holes (erasing restores a = 1, b = 0, which here is a hole): small ones settle into negatons for skates to hit, long strokes become worms.
